title: Review: Membrane structure (fluid mosaic); Diffusion and facilitated diffusion; Prokaryotic cells and viruses; Osmosis and water potential
source: Questions copied unchanged from the mission-lesson scripts for AP Biology (status of the source: mission-lesson scripts of Oct-Nov 2026 (reviewed by AI reviewers; not signed off by a person)). Terms and clues: CE04b#t2 term and clue written for the game; CE04b#t4 term and clue written for the game; MB03a#t4 term and clue written for the game; MB02a#t2 term and clue written for the game. Questions: CE04a#N.3b, CE04b#N.2b, MB01b#N.13, MB02a#N.12, MB03a#N.9b, CE04a#N.5b, CE04b#N.16, MB02a#N.7b, MB03a#N.10, CE04b#N.11. Some questions repeat from the worlds it reviews.

assemble.prompt: Match each term to its definition.

items.label: Bacteriophage
items.clue: Virus with DNA in a protein head and a protein tail that injects the DNA

items.label: Acellular
items.clue: Having no cytoplasm and no ribosomes, as is true of every virus particle

items.label: Turgor pressure
items.clue: Push of the cell contents on the wall after water has entered a walled cell.

items.label: Facilitated diffusion
items.clue: Passive net movement down a concentration gradient through a membrane protein.

questions.stem: Which statement best describes how the DNA of a typical prokaryotic cell is organized?

options.text: It is enclosed in a nucleus by a nuclear envelope, just as in eukaryotic cells.
It is spread evenly through the cytoplasm, with no region set aside for it.
It is concentrated in a nucleoid region, which is not enclosed by a membrane.
It is held inside small membrane-bound organelles, such as mitochondria.

questions.explanation: Prokaryotic cells typically lack a nucleus; their DNA is concentrated in a nucleoid region, a specialized internal region without a surrounding membrane.

questions.stem: Tobacco mosaic virus consists of a protein coat surrounding a single RNA molecule; it contains no DNA. When it infects tobacco cells, new virus particles are made, each with the same genetic information as the infecting virus. Which statement best explains how this virus stores and passes on its genetic information?

options.text: Its RNA molecule stores the genetic information that is passed to new viruses.
Its protein coat stores the genetic information that is passed on to new viruses.
It uses the tobacco cell's DNA, as only DNA can store genetic information.
Its genetic information is kept in a nucleus inside each virus particle.

questions.stem: A student claims that proteins in the plasma membrane can move sideways within the membrane. Which observation would best support this claim?

options.text: As the cell grows, the total amount of protein in its plasma membrane increases steadily.
When fluorescent proteins in one small patch are permanently bleached, the patch glows again within a minute.
Micrographs show proteins scattered among the phospholipids rather than forming a separate layer.
Proteins labelled on the outer surface of the plasma membrane are later found inside the cytosol.

questions.stem: A hypothetical toxin binds to and blocks all of the channel and transport proteins in the plasma membrane of a cell. Which prediction about the cell, immediately after exposure to the toxin, is best supported?

options.text: Its uptake of both glucose and O₂ will stop, since all substances cross through proteins.
Its glucose uptake will not change, since glucose passes freely through the phospholipid bilayer.
Its glucose uptake will rise through other routes to meet the cell's own need for glucose.
Its glucose uptake will fall sharply, while O₂ will still diffuse in across the bilayer.

questions.stem: A freshwater protist lives in pond water that is hypotonic to its cytoplasm. The protist has a contractile vacuole that repeatedly fills and then empties to the outside of the cell. Which statement best explains why the protist needs its contractile vacuole?

options.text: Water keeps leaving by osmosis, and the vacuole stores water to replace the loss.
Salts keep leaving the cell by osmosis, and the vacuole takes in salt to replace the loss.
Water cannot cross the cell membrane, so the vacuole brings in all the water it needs.
Osmosis brings water into the cell steadily, and the vacuole expels the excess water.

questions.stem: Cells of baker's yeast often contain many copies of a small circular DNA molecule that is located in the nucleus but is not part of any of the yeast's linear chromosomes. Which statement about this molecule is correct?

options.text: It is not a plasmid, as plasmids are a feature of prokaryotic cells.
It shows that yeast is a prokaryote, as circular DNA is a prokaryotic feature.
It is a plasmid, as plasmids occur in eukaryotes as well as in prokaryotes.
It carries no genes, as genes are carried on the yeast's chromosomes.

questions.explanation: A plasmid is an extra-chromosomal circular DNA molecule. Plasmids are best known in prokaryotes, but eukaryotes can contain them too, and this yeast molecule is one.

questions.stem: A population of a hypothetical soil bacterium contains no cells resistant to antibiotic Z. A few of its cells receive, by conjugation with cells of another bacterial species, a plasmid carrying a gene for resistance to Z. Which statement best describes the effect of this transfer on the population?

options.text: Its genetic variation is unchanged, as only a new mutation can add a new gene
Every cell becomes resistant at once, as transferred genes spread to all cells together
Recipient cells fuse with donor cells, making offspring with genes of both species
Its genetic variation increases, as it gains a gene from another species

questions.stem: Cells of a hypothetical animal take up Na⁺ from the fluid around them by facilitated diffusion. Which statement best describes how the Na⁺ ions cross the plasma membrane?

options.text: They diffuse through a channel protein, from high to low Na⁺ concentration.
They slip directly between the phospholipids, as the ions are small enough to fit.
They are pushed across by a channel protein that uses ATP to move each ion in.
They pass through a one-way channel protein that lets ions enter the cell only.

questions.explanation: Facilitated diffusion of an ion is passive movement through a channel, down the ion's concentration gradient. No ATP is used.

questions.stem: Jam contains so much sugar that most bacteria landing on it cannot grow. Which statement explains this?

options.text: Sugar diffuses into the bacteria until there is enough inside them to poison them.
Water leaves the bacteria by osmosis into the jam, so their cytoplasm shrinks and they cannot grow.
Water enters the bacteria from the jam, so the bacteria swell up and burst.
Their cell walls stop any water from crossing, so the bacteria cannot take in water.

questions.explanation: The jam is far more concentrated than the cytoplasm. Water leaves the cells by osmosis; the contents shrink away from the wall, and without water the cells cannot grow.

questions.stem: A hypothetical drug is proposed to block reverse transcriptase. Researchers add the drug to human cells in culture and then expose the cells to a retrovirus. If the drug works as proposed, which result is predicted?

options.text: New viral proteins are still made, because ribosomes translate the viral RNA genome directly.
The cells stop transcribing their own genes, because the drug blocks their transcription enzyme.
The virus switches to copying its RNA directly into new RNA, since it needs to go on reproducing.
Viral RNA enters the cells, but no viral DNA is made, so no new viral progeny are assembled.
